provenance: Editorial TOPIK II Level 6 grammar selection including formal and literary recognition patterns; NOT an official TOPIK checklist; educator review required.

grammarPoints.title: N(으)로 말미암아
grammarPoints.hint: Give a cause in formal, literary or official writing: 'due to / arising from'.
grammarPoints.description: Give a cause in formal, literary or official writing: 'due to / arising from'. It states a cause in elevated written or literary Korean.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach (으)로 말미암아 to the causal noun: 사고로 말미암아, 변화로 말미암아.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 재해로 말미암아 피해가 커졌어요. — Damage increased due to the disaster. 재해로 말미암아 makes the disaster the formal explanation of the damage.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: It is far more formal than 때문에; don't use it as your ordinary conversational 'because'.

lessonExamples.englishHint: Damage increased due to the disaster.
The road closed due to an accident.

cards.englishHint: Many people left because of war.
Problems arose due to climate change.
Poor communication deepened the conflict.

grammarPoints.title: N을/를 막론하고
grammarPoints.hint: Say that a conclusion is true regardless of which member of a group is involved.
grammarPoints.description: Say that a conclusion is true regardless of which member of a group is involved. It says the distinction named is irrelevant to the outcome.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 을/를 막론하고 to the named distinction: 나이를 막론하고.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 나이를 막론하고 누구나 참여할 수 있어요. — Anyone can join regardless of age. 나이를 막론하고 means age does not affect whether anyone can participate.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This states that a distinction is irrelevant; it does not mark a cause or an exception.

lessonExamples.fullSentence: 나이를 막론하고 누구나 참여할 수 있어요.
lessonExamples.englishHint: Anyone can join regardless of age.
Anyone can apply regardless of gender.

cards.englishHint: Everyone is welcome regardless of nationality.
Anyone can apply regardless of age.
Interest is high across all regions.

grammarPoints.title: -거니와
grammarPoints.hint: Add a second supporting fact: 'not only A but also B', often in formal writing.
grammarPoints.description: Add a second supporting fact: 'not only A but also B', often in formal writing. It adds another argument or feature in a literary or formal style.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 거니와 to a predicate stem; the next clause adds another fact.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 시간이 부족하거니와 비용도 많이 듭니다. — Time is short and the cost is high as well. 시간이 부족하거니와 비용도 많이 듭니다 gives two reasons against the plan.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: It is elevated and additive; not a neutral replacement for every casual 그리고.

lessonExamples.englishHint: Time is short and the cost is high as well.
The problem is complex and hard to solve.

cards.englishHint: He's diligent and highly capable too.
The scenery is nice and the air is clear too.
The content matters and wording must be precise.

grammarPoints.title: -기에 이르다
grammarPoints.hint: Describe how events eventually reached a particular outcome or stage.
grammarPoints.description: Describe how events eventually reached a particular outcome or stage. It presents a development as reaching a particular stage or endpoint.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 기에 이르다 to the action verb describing the final outcome.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 결국 사직하기에 이르렀어요. — Eventually I came to resign. 사직하기에 이르렀어요 says circumstances culminated in resignation.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is a formal endpoint construction, not a synonym for wanting to do something.

lessonExamples.englishHint: Eventually I came to resign.
The conflict escalated until there was a lawsuit.

cards.englishHint: Eventually I achieved the goal after much effort.
The discussion eventually reached agreement.
Things worsened until the business closed.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄹ지언정
grammarPoints.hint: Declare a principle that will stand even if an unfavorable event occurs.
grammarPoints.description: Declare a principle that will stand even if an unfavorable event occurs. It expresses a strong 'even if' concession while preserving a firm stance.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach -(으)ㄹ지언정 to the conceded possibility, then assert the commitment.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 실패할지언정 포기하지 않겠습니다. — Even if I fail, I won't give up. 실패할지언정 포기하지 않겠습니다 puts refusal to give up above the possibility of failure.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: More emphatic and literary than -더라도; use it for strongly held positions.

lessonExamples.englishHint: Even if I fail, I won't give up.
Even if I lose money, I'll keep my promise.

cards.englishHint: Even if criticized, I'll tell the truth.
Even if left alone, I won't yield.
Even if late, I won't overdo it.

grammarPoints.title: -기는 하되
grammarPoints.hint: Admit one fact but place a clear qualification or limit on it.
grammarPoints.description: Admit one fact but place a clear qualification or limit on it. It accepts one point but places a restriction on the next.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 기는 하되 to the action or descriptive stem, followed by the restriction.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 인정하기는 하되 동의하지는 않아요. — I acknowledge it but don't agree. 인정하기는 하되 동의하지는 않아요 accepts a point while rejecting full agreement.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is not a simple additive 'and'; the second clause qualifies the first.

lessonExamples.englishHint: I acknowledge it but don't agree.
I'll help, but won't do it for you.

cards.englishHint: I'll attend, but can't stay long.
I'll allow it, but there are conditions.
I'll publish it but keep the names private.

grammarPoints.title: -다손 치더라도
grammarPoints.hint: Concede a hypothetical claim while resisting its conclusion; change -다손 to -ㄴ다손/-는다손 after action verbs.
grammarPoints.description: This formal argumentative concession temporarily grants a premise without accepting the resulting conclusion. Descriptive predicates use -다손 치더라도, whereas action verbs require -ㄴ다손 or -는다손 according to their final sound.
grammarPoints.structurePattern: [Descriptive stem] + -다손 치더라도; [Action verb vowel/ㄹ stem] + -ㄴ다손 치더라도; [Action verb other consonant stem] + -는다손 치더라도

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Descriptive: 싸다 → 싸다손 치더라도. Action verb with vowel stem: 가다 → 간다손 치더라도, 출발하다 → 출발한다손 치더라도. Action verb with consonant stem: 먹다 → 먹는다손 치더라도. Keep a space before 치더라도.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 싸다손 치더라도 지금 살 필요는 없어요. — Even if it is cheap, there's no need to buy it now. The cheap price is granted but does not justify a purchase.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Do not add bare -다손 to an action verb: 먹다손 is not the intended form (먹는다손). The clause after 치더라도 must show why granting the premise does not settle the point.

lessonExamples.fullSentence: 싸다손 치더라도 지금 살 필요는 없어요.
lessonExamples.englishHint: Even if it is cheap, there's no need to buy it now.

lessonExamples.fullSentence: 그 말이 맞다손 치더라도 문제가 남아요.
lessonExamples.englishHint: Even if that claim is right, problems remain.

cards.englishHint: Even if you're busy, you should still call.

cards.fullSentence: 일찍 출발한다손 치더라도 제시간에 도착하기는 어려워요.
cards.englishHint: Even if we set off early, arriving on time will still be difficult.

cards.fullSentence: 많이 먹는다손 치더라도 음식이 남을 거예요.
cards.englishHint: Even if we eat a lot, some food will remain.

grammarPoints.title: -기로서니
grammarPoints.hint: Criticize behavior as unacceptable even after granting a reason: 'however X, how could Y?'.
grammarPoints.description: Criticize behavior as unacceptable even after granting a reason: 'however X, how could Y?'. It reproaches someone: even granting the situation, their action remains unacceptable.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 기로서니 to the stated reason or condition, then question the excessive response.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 아무리 바쁘기로서니 연락도 안 하다니요? — However busy you are, how can you not call? 아무리 바쁘기로서니 연락도 안 하다니요? criticizes not calling even if busy.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Usually expresses disbelief or reproach; not a neutral written conditional.

lessonExamples.englishHint: However busy you are, how can you not call?
However angry you are, that was too harsh.

cards.englishHint: However close you are, manners still matter.
However hard it is, you shouldn't quit.
However urgent it is, rules still apply.

grammarPoints.title: -느니 차라리
grammarPoints.hint: Express a strong preference: 'rather than doing X, I'd sooner do Y'.
grammarPoints.description: Express a strong preference: 'rather than doing X, I'd sooner do Y'. It prefers one action rather than pursuing a worse alternative.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Put 느니 after the rejected verb and 차라리 before the preferred alternative.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 기다리느니 차라리 걸어가겠어요. — I'd rather walk than wait. 기다리느니 차라리 걸어가겠어요 explicitly chooses walking over waiting.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Unlike -거나, it rejects one option and favors another; the tone can be forceful.

lessonExamples.englishHint: I'd rather walk than wait.
I'd rather try than regret it.

cards.englishHint: I'd rather be silent than lie.
I'd rather start again than quit.
I'd rather go tomorrow than go late.

grammarPoints.title: N은/는 고사하고
grammarPoints.hint: Reject even a basic expectation: 'let alone / far from'.
grammarPoints.description: Reject even a basic expectation: 'let alone / far from'. It excludes the first item as well as the following, more basic item.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 은/는 고사하고 to the higher expectation, then mention the even lesser reality.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 감사는 고사하고 사과조차 없었어요. — There wasn't even an apology, let alone thanks. 감사는 고사하고 사과조차 없었어요 says there was not even an apology, much less gratitude.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This reverses the scale of expectations and is emphatic; it is not ordinary noun coordination.

lessonExamples.englishHint: There wasn't even an apology, let alone thanks.
I worked weekends, let alone taking vacations.

cards.fullSentence: 승리는 고사하고 한 점도 못 냈어요.
cards.englishHint: We couldn't score, let alone win.
We don't know the cause, let alone a solution.
I got obstruction, let alone help.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)려야 -(으)ㄹ 수 없다
grammarPoints.hint: Say that doing something is impossible despite any effort or desire to do it.
grammarPoints.description: Say that doing something is impossible despite any effort or desire to do it. It emphasizes that the action cannot be achieved however hard one tries.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Repeat the verb as -(으)려야 and -(으)ㄹ 수 없다: 피하다 → 피하려야 피할 수 없다.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 이제는 피하려야 피할 수 없어요. — There's no way to avoid it now. 피하려야 피할 수 없어요 means avoiding the problem is impossible however much one tries.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is emphatic inability, not a neutral future prediction or lack of knowledge.

lessonExamples.englishHint: There's no way to avoid it now.
I can't forget it however hard I try.

cards.englishHint: I can't bring myself to believe it.
I simply can't hold it in.
It cannot be stopped no matter what.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)나 마나
grammarPoints.hint: Say that doing or not doing an action would make no difference.
grammarPoints.description: Say that doing or not doing an action would make no difference. It states that doing the action is pointless because the result is unchanged.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach -(으)나 마나 to the action stem: 보다 → 보나 마나, 물어보다 → 물어보나 마나.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 물어보나 마나 거절할 거예요. — They'll refuse whether you ask or not. 물어보나 마나 거절할 거예요 means asking is pointless because refusal is certain.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This predicts an unchanged outcome; -거나 merely lists alternatives and does not signal futility.

lessonExamples.englishHint: They'll refuse whether you ask or not.
Going or not won't change the result.

cards.fullSentence: 읽으나 마나 이해 못 할 거예요.
cards.englishHint: Reading it won't help me understand.
They won't come whether you wait or not.
Even trying it won't change the failure.

grammarPoints.title: -기 짝이 없다
grammarPoints.hint: State that a quality is extremely strong, often an unpleasant one.
grammarPoints.description: State that a quality is extremely strong, often an unpleasant one. It expresses a strongly negative or extreme evaluation.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 기 짝이 없다 to a descriptive stem: 불쾌하다 → 불쾌하기 짝이 없다.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 그 태도는 무책임하기 짝이 없어요. — That attitude is utterly irresponsible. 무책임하기 짝이 없어요 emphasizes an extreme level of irresponsibility.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is emphatic and literary, not a neutral description of mild discomfort.

lessonExamples.englishHint: That attitude is utterly irresponsible.
That remark is extremely offensive.

cards.englishHint: The situation is terribly regrettable.
That behavior is utterly foolish.
That explanation is extremely inaccurate.

grammarPoints.title: -기 일쑤이다
grammarPoints.hint: Describe a frequently repeated, usually unwanted habit or outcome.
grammarPoints.description: Describe a frequently repeated, usually unwanted habit or outcome. It says an undesirable action occurs repeatedly or habitually.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Add 기 일쑤이다 to the action verb stem and conjugate it: 늦다 → 늦기 일쑤예요.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 그는 약속을 잊기 일쑤예요. — He keeps forgetting appointments. 약속을 잊기 일쑤예요 says forgetting appointments happens far too often.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is not neutral habitual -곤 하다; it usually carries criticism or an unwanted pattern.

lessonExamples.englishHint: He keeps forgetting appointments.
I often end up late after sleeping late.

cards.englishHint: I frequently make mistakes when unprepared.
Eating too fast often gives me indigestion.
I keep forgetting my password.

grammarPoints.title: -다 못해
grammarPoints.hint: An action or feeling reaches a limit and leads to another action.
grammarPoints.description: An action or feeling reaches a limit and leads to another action. It describes emotion or behavior becoming so intense that it exceeds normal limits.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 다 못해 to the action or state stem, then say what happens when the limit is reached.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 참다 못해 소리쳤어요. — I couldn't stand it and shouted. 참다 못해 소리쳤어요 says patience ran out and shouting resulted.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: The phrase is not merely negation of ability; it marks a breaking point or excess.

lessonExamples.englishHint: I couldn't stand it and shouted.
I finally called after waiting too long.

cards.englishHint: I became so angry I cried.
I was so worried I went there myself.
I became so frustrated I went outside.

grammarPoints.title: -아/어 대다
grammarPoints.hint: Describe someone doing an action repeatedly and excessively, often annoyingly.
grammarPoints.description: Describe someone doing an action repeatedly and excessively, often annoyingly. It describes actions being carried out repeatedly, often excessively or noisily.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 대다 after the verb's 아/어 form: 울다 → 울어 대다.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 아이들이 떠들어 댔어요. — The children kept making a racket. 아이들이 떠들어 댔어요 suggests noisy, excessive repeated talking.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Not a neutral continuous action like -고 있다; it usually conveys excess or irritation.

lessonExamples.englishHint: The children kept making a racket.
The dog kept barking noisily.

cards.englishHint: The baby kept crying loudly.
He kept complaining.
People bombarded me with questions.

grammarPoints.title: -다시피 하다
grammarPoints.hint: Express that an action happens almost completely or practically to an extreme.
grammarPoints.description: Express that an action happens almost completely or practically to an extreme. It expresses that someone almost does an action or does it to a great degree.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 다시피 하다 to an action stem: 살다 → 살다시피 하다.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 매일 밤을 새우다시피 했어요. — I practically stayed up every night. 매일 밤을 새우다시피 했어요 describes staying up almost every night.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Different from -다시피 ('as you know'), which asks the listener to recognize evidence.

lessonExamples.englishHint: I practically stayed up every night.
He practically ran all day.

cards.englishHint: I practically lived in the library before exams.
I was practically standing through the meeting.
I practically skipped meals because I was busy.

grammarPoints.title: -다시피 (as you can see)
grammarPoints.hint: Refer to evidence already visible or known to the listener: 'as you know / as you saw'.
grammarPoints.description: Use -다시피 after a perception or knowledge verb to point to something the listener can see, hear, or already knows. This evidence-appeal construction differs in meaning from the 'practically / almost' pattern -다시피 하다.
grammarPoints.structurePattern: [Perception/knowledge verb stem (알다, 보다, 듣다)] + -다시피; often with honorific -시-

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 다시피 after a perception verb such as 보다, 알다 or 듣다.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 보시다시피 결과가 달라졌어요. — As you can see, the results changed. 보시다시피 결과가 달라졌어요 points to results the listener can already see.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is not the extreme-frequency meaning of -다시피 하다; the two must be taught separately.

lessonExamples.englishHint: As you can see, the results changed.
As you know, we're short on time.

cards.englishHint: As you can see, preparations are done.
As everyone knows, the rules changed.
As you can see, the situation is serious.

grammarPoints.title: -기에 망정이지
grammarPoints.hint: Say that a fortunate cause prevented a worse result: 'it's a good thing X happened'.
grammarPoints.description: Say that a fortunate cause prevented a worse result: 'it's a good thing X happened'. It says that something fortunately happened, preventing an unfavorable alternative.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 기에 망정이지 to the fortunate condition, then mention the danger avoided.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 일찍 출발했기에 망정이지 늦을 뻔했어요. — Luckily we left early; otherwise we'd be late. 일찍 출발했기에 망정이지 늦을 뻔했어요 says the early departure prevented lateness.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Typically contrasts the fortunate fact with a bad counterfactual; it is not ordinary because.

lessonExamples.englishHint: Luckily we left early; otherwise we'd be late.
Luckily you helped; I couldn't do it alone.

cards.fullSentence: 미리 알았기에 망정이지 큰일 날 뻔했어요.
cards.englishHint: Luckily I knew beforehand; it could've been awful.

cards.fullSentence: 돈이 있었기에 망정이지 못 샀을 거예요.
cards.englishHint: Luckily I had money, or I couldn't have bought it.
Luckily I wasn't late, or I'd have missed it.

grammarPoints.title: -는가 하면
grammarPoints.hint: Contrast different situations within one topic: 'on one hand..., on the other...'.
grammarPoints.description: Contrast different situations within one topic: 'on one hand..., on the other...'. It juxtaposes different situations or behaviors, sometimes within one subject.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 는가 하면 to an action predicate; descriptive forms can use -(으)ㄴ가 하면.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 어떤 사람은 찬성하는가 하면 다른 사람은 반대해요. — Some agree, while others oppose. 찬성하는가 하면 반대해요 introduces opposing reactions among different people.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is more structured written contrast than the everyday sentence starter 하지만.

lessonExamples.fullSentence: 어떤 사람은 찬성하는가 하면 다른 사람은 반대해요.
lessonExamples.englishHint: Some agree, while others oppose.

lessonExamples.fullSentence: 날씨가 맑은가 하면 갑자기 비가 와요.
lessonExamples.englishHint: It is sunny one moment and rainy the next.

cards.englishHint: He laughs, then suddenly cries.

cards.fullSentence: 지역에 따라 인구가 느는가 하면 줄기도 해요.
cards.englishHint: Population grows in some regions and shrinks in others.

cards.fullSentence: 어떤 곳은 붐비는가 하면 다른 곳은 조용해요.
cards.englishHint: Some places are crowded, others quiet.

grammarPoints.title: -기 나름이다
grammarPoints.hint: Say an outcome depends on how someone approaches or handles an action.
grammarPoints.description: Say an outcome depends on how someone approaches or handles an action. It makes the result depend on how a person approaches the task.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 기 나름이다 to an action stem: 생각하다 → 생각하기 나름이다.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 행복은 생각하기 나름이에요. — Happiness depends on how you think. 행복은 생각하기 나름이에요 says happiness depends on one's perspective.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: It does not promise that all outcomes are under personal control; it highlights variation by method.

lessonExamples.englishHint: Happiness depends on how you think.
The outcome depends on effort.

cards.englishHint: This tool depends on how you use it.
The evaluation depends on interpretation.
The problem depends on how you approach it.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄹ 법도 하다
grammarPoints.hint: Say that a feeling, action or outcome would be understandable or plausible.
grammarPoints.description: Say that a feeling, action or outcome would be understandable or plausible. It states that a certain outcome or behavior would be reasonable or unsurprising.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach -(으)ㄹ 법도 하다 to the predicate stem and conjugate 하다.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 그렇게 느낄 법도 해요. — It's understandable to feel that way. 그렇게 느낄 법도 해요 grants that the reaction is understandable.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Compare with -(으)ㄹ 리가 없다, which denies a possibility rather than allowing it.

lessonExamples.englishHint: It's understandable to feel that way.
It's understandable to believe that.

cards.englishHint: It's natural to be angry.
It's understandable that they were surprised.
It's the kind of situation where mistakes are understandable.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)리라
grammarPoints.hint: Express a solemn prediction, resolution or conviction in literary/formal style.
grammarPoints.description: Express a solemn prediction, resolution or conviction in literary/formal style. It conveys a literary prediction or solemn resolve about the future.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach -(으)리라 to the stem: 이루다 → 이루리라, 끝나다 → 끝나리라.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 언젠가 꿈을 이루리라 믿습니다. — I believe I'll fulfill my dream one day. 언젠가 이루리라 믿습니다 voices a firm, almost literary conviction of eventual success.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is not the normal spoken future -ㄹ 거예요, and it can sound dramatic in conversation.

lessonExamples.englishHint: I believe I'll fulfill my dream one day.
I believe everything will pass.

cards.englishHint: I believe the truth will emerge.
I expect peace will come eventually.
I believe the effort will bear fruit.

grammarPoints.title: -노라면
grammarPoints.hint: Present what one comes to realize or encounter while continuing an action over time.
grammarPoints.description: Present what one comes to realize or encounter while continuing an action over time. It describes an eventual result from continuing an action over time.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 노라면 to an action stem, then mention the outcome that emerges with time.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 계속 걷노라면 길이 보일 거예요. — As you keep walking, a path will appear. 계속 걷노라면 길이 보일 거예요 depicts sustained walking until a path appears.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Literary and reflective: everyday Korean would usually use -다 보면 instead.

lessonExamples.englishHint: As you keep walking, a path will appear.
Through living long, you learn many things.

cards.englishHint: As I keep reading, time flies.
As I listen to music, I relax.
As you keep waiting, good news will come.
